entities.summary:
The Board of Peace is listed in contemporary reference data as an international organisation associated with Washington, D.C., and a founding date of 2026—an emerging or prospective institution in peace-related governance rather than a long-established treaty organisation. Sparse public institutional history means its profile is still forming in diplomatic directories.

If operationalised along typical NGO/IGO hybrid lines, such boards usually convene experts, track conflicts, and issue recommendations without independent coercive power. Their significance depends on member buy-in, funding, and recognition by states and the UN system.

As a nascent entity, the Board of Peace illustrates how new peace-architecture brands continually appear at the edges of formal international organisation.
